Justice Insulted: The Murray family's search for closure

By: Joy Summers | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
While the Murray family wait for cops to investigate the assassination of Thomas and Cloete Murray, it seems the generals in charge of their investigation were lining their pockets with bribes from cr

Unique Selling Point:
We have two family members and Witness A B and C at the commission which puts a different spin on the story

Summary:
It’s been two years and eight months since Cloete Murray and his son Thomas were assassinated on the NI highway near Midrand on a Saturday afternoon.

Thomas and his father had been working on a multimillion-rand case for Investec and they had left Melrose Arch and were travelling home. What they did not realize is that they were followed and gunned down by three men in a bakkie near the New Road offramp.

The family have been shattered, but they are healing as best they can. The police have been appalling despite promises from two of the nation’s top cops, General Shadrack Sibiya and Richard Shiburi.
These two generals promised the family justice after the first law enforcement team failed them.

But they have failed them too and now perhaps we know why. In the last few weeks, startling revelations from the Madlanga commission suggest that these men were busy lining their pockets from a man accused of looting Thembisa hospital and attempting to murder his girlfriend. While the allegations remain untested and come from a man accused of serious crimes, the level of detail that were given to three law enforcement officers by Cat Matlala is startling.


Further information:
But back to the Murray family who have revealed that the assassins are known to them as they have the evidence. And yet still no arrests have been made. Carte Blanche goes into the anatomy of an investigation that will reveal the deep flaws in our criminal justice system and tracks the heartbreak and healing of the Murray family over the last 32 months as they have tried everything to get justice and closure. It also looks at the other whistleblowers who have been assassinated in that time.

Justice Insulted| The Murray Murders 2025 FINAL SCRIPT Fact checked and fixed version for voice over

Voice over One
In 2023 Cloete Murray was ruffling feathers.

One of the country’s top liquidators, he was involved in high profile State Capture cases and other multimillion rand estates.

Murray had a nose for finding well hidden assets and cash, a skill that didn’t go down well in the dark tangled criminal landscapes of Gauteng

James Murray
There is a WhatsApp group of ..I don’t know how to put it, the devil’s favourite children. They don’t necessarily discuss my father, but they discuss all sorts of unsanitary things

Voice over 2
James Murray and his younger brother Thomas worked with their father.

Title: Saturday 18th March 2023

On a March morning more than two years ago, Thomas joined Cloete to assess three properties of a company called B.I.G- Business Innovations Group that had allegedly defrauded Investec bank of millions.

It was Thomas’ first liquidation. His wife Monet was going to join them but stayed at home to look after their 6 month old son

Monet Murray
He was excited about that, you know he was really crossing his T’s and dotting his I’s.

Voice over 3
These are the last known images of Thomas and Cloete, captured by cameras outside the Pretoria home of Rushil Singh one of the B.I.G directors. From this address they’d travelled to the exclusive Melrose Arch shopping district.

Govan
What stands out for you from that day?
Monet Murray
Thomas was, he assisted his father with a lot of large matters, dangerous matters, but that week he was very anxious. When he was brushing his teeth, he told me, do you know where to scatter my ashes, and I was like okay well we used to joke around, and he was like “no do you really know where to scatter my ashes. “So, there was something different to him.

Voice over 4
At around two in the afternoon, on the N1 highway, near Midrand north of Joburg, a white Ford Ranger pulled up alongside them.

Up sound shots

13 bullets were pumped into their vehicle.

shots

Thomas died on the scene, shot through the heart, the lungs and the arm. Cloete succumbed to his injuries later in hospital.

Monet
The other day my son asked me daddy where are you? Pappa where are you?
Govan
Regtig?
I have a little cross around my neck, and every night I would tell him, its for Daddy. For pappa, and he would say “kruisie papa” and then he said “Pappa where are you? “That’s difficult!
Govan
Oh my gosh Monet.

James Murray
I can only imagine what my brothers last thirty seconds must have been like. I know he was in excruciating pain. They were on the phone with a good friend of my father, and he told me they were laughing and then he heard these cracks, and he just heard my brother scream: eina! Eina! Eina!
Govan whispers
Ah man…
James
And then it went silent, and he could just hear my father (breathes) obviously going into some form of instinctive breathing at that point

Voice over 5
James and his mother raced to the scene.

James Murray
We drove as fast as we could hazards on, were just honked the horn. We took the offramp, the big bird offramp. I stopped the vehicle, I jumped out of the car, and I just started running across the highway

James
I thought it was an accident.

Voice over 6
This was the brutal scene that confronted him.

James
I wasn’t looking at the windows, I was looking at my brother and, on my way back, I realized oh.... those are bullet holes.

Voice over 7
Only then did James realise his father and brother had been assassinated.

James
At that point we didn’t know which one of my father’s high-profile cases was the one that led to this. If you had to ask me on that day, was it the B.I.G case? I would say, I doubt it, there were many other people that wanted my father dead.

Voice over 8
The killer is still at large, and a family dealt a double trauma is no closer to finding closure. More than two years later, we ask, why?

Fade to black

Voice over 9
It was a double murder that made international headlines and rocked the country’s liquidations sector.

As speculation on a possible motive for the killing spread, bringing the killers to book fell to Brigadier Pulane (Pauline) Gopane, the head of organized crime in Gauteng.

James
The joke is what investigation?

Voice over 10
At first the family gave Brigadier Gopane’s team the benefit of the doubt, but later they watched them bungle almost every aspect of the investigation

James Murray
I have obviously been privy to quite a bit of what they have done, but if you were to write a book of how to not investigate murder, you could just run this down, play by play.


LINK
The Murray murders are an uncomfortable reminder of everything that is wrong in this criminal justice system, and driving past the scene of the assassination, leaves a bitter taste every time.

Voice over 11
News24’s investigative journalist, Kyle Cowan, has been following the story for the past two and a half years.

The long list of shortcomings began when HE discovered a file in Cloete’s car, mistakenly left behind by the police.

Govan
So, you assumed the police would have taken it?
Kyle
That would have been my first thing, go through the car! Ballistic evidence was left behind in the car, the house keys were left behind in the car. That file would have given them, on day one, on the day of the shootings would have told them, these are the people that these guys they were interacting with, minutes, hours, before they were killed.
Govan
So, the investigation into who killed Cloete and Thomas Murray started with mistakes?
Kyle
It starts with a mistake within hours of the shootings happening.
This file was eventually collected by the family.

Voice over 12
From the outset, the investigation, according to Cowan, was beset by delays.

Kyle
So everything that should take a couple of days, filing subpoenas for cell phone records, takes two months.

Voice over 13
Because it was high profile, two officers from the Directorate for Priority Crime, or Hawks, joined the team. A suspect was identified days after the murders.

James
There was one gent in that team, from the DPCI, that was extremely competent, and he was essentially doing everything, if he wasn’t there, they wouldn’t even have identified Barwell.



Kyle
They identify a guy called Ryan Barwell. He’s captured on CCTV cameras at Melrose Arch.

Up sound

Kyle Cowan
Cloete Murray and his son Thomas drive in, right behind them is an auctioneer, and the third vehicle is a white Ford Ranger bakkie being driven by Ryan Barwell.
Govan
So why is he following the Murrays?
Kyle
What we figured out is that Barwell has very close ties to the same people who the Murray’s were liquidating on behalf of Investec Bank.

VO 14
Cameras on the N1 highway also confirmed the vehicle used by the assailants, was a white Ford Ranger.

Kyle
We are looking at a white Ford Ranger without number plates being driven by Ryan Barwell appearing to follow the Murrays into the Melrose Arch parking garage.

Within two hours a same white Ford Ranger is involved in the shooting, and that is captured on camera.

VO 15
Shockingly, instead of swiftly acting on the information, James says, Brigadier Gopane removed the Hawks investigators.

James Murray
And then the investigation grinds to a halt.
Govan
So she wanted to fire the people doing the work?
James
That is correct. It was a political exercise

VO16
It also emerged that the prime suspect had never been questioned.

Govan
The police have never interviewed Ryan Barwell. Why not!
Kyle
Never! I don’t understand to this day why Brig Gopane team failed to interview him.

VO 17
Ryan Barwell has a R9 million default judgement against him from SARS, perhaps that’s why WE can’t find him to ask him for his right of reply.

Kyle continues
Ryan Barwell may not be a suspect in the murders, but he was driving a vehicle that you can forensically match to the vehicle used in the murders – so this person would be your number one witness. He can tell you who was in that car with them that day. At the very least you can exclude him as a suspect. They haven’t even done that!

Voice over 18
On the day of their murder, Cloete and Thomas were writing up the assets of the B.I.G group. Two of the company’s directors were Rushil and Nishani Singh. Rushil is a highflyer known for driving high end sports cars. His sister Nishani has since died.

James
So, they get an arrest warrant for Rushil Singh, they don’t arrest him. It takes them months, they tell us they can’t find him, and they can’t speak to crime intelligence because they don’t trust crime intelligence, so they can’t find him. So, I tell them, he lives with his mother, go to his house, and they just do nothing.
Govan
At that point other people outside of the police, were starting to put the pieces together.
James
Yes that is correct.
Govan
Was that information reaching the police?
James
Yes, in droves! They had been given notes and information and photos and bank statements, and vehicle transfer records.

Voice over 19
It’s evidence, the Murray family believes links the Singh siblings to the assassination.

LINK
By 2024 the police had been handed the evidence, but instead of acting on it, they chose to do something no one saw coming

Voice over 20
James was called in after News 24’s scathing articles about the investigation. He realised then, he was now a suspect, based on his cell phone calls to his brother Thomas.

James
They knew who drove the vehicle, they know which vehicle did it, they to an extent know who was in the vehicle, at least one of the three people, and at this point based on phone calls between my brother and myself which they think are between my father and myself, they decided that I am a suspect in this murder case, because for some reason they reckon that I would have been a beneficiary of this absolute life destroying event

Voice over 21
James filed a complaint to the police, and in what first appeared to be a promising move, the national head of organized crime, Major General Richard Shibiri, was assigned to the case.

Kyle
At this point he appears to be the guy who can maybe change the fortunes of this investigation.

Voice Over 22
But there’s a reason that name sounds familiar.

Last month, the Madlanga Commission of Inquiry into corruption and interference in our criminal justice system, heard that General Shibiri is accused of taking bribes in another murder investigation. Accusations he’s strongly denied.

Kyle
We end 2024 effectively in exactly the same place where we ended the year before.

Up sound page turn

Kyle
The two-year anniversary, by March 2025, the family start becoming angry.

Voice over 23
Cowan prepared yet another report, and sent his questions to the police

Kyle
They then tell me they have recovered the Ford Ranger, the suspect vehicle, the one that was used in the murders. I go to the police impound and I take pictures of the vehicle. That’s in March. They wait until September to start doing anything to this vehicle.

Voice over 24
It appears, though, to have been the wrong vehicle.

Govan
So was that car ever found?
Kyle
They are never going to find that car Govan. That car is gone
Govan
Besides the vehicle, they have some idea of who the suspects could be, right?
Kyle
Yes, so remember back in 2023 people had already figured out Barwell was driving the car, and there are identities of other possible occupants that were given to the police. They have known for two years at this point

Voice over 25
This year, an image of the man in the front seat of the Ford Ranger on the day of the murder was published.

Govan
At this point I am not surprised that they didn’t go and ask him to prove that wasn’t him, leaning forward.
Kyle
Ya and now they can’t anymore.
Govan
Why?
Kyle
Because on the first of October he was killed.

Voice over 26
Burnett Hermanus was gunned down outside a Joburg hospital last month.

Up sound shots

Kyle
Burnett Hermanus is the guy we suspect was in the front passenger seat of that white Ford Ranger. The guy who shot them.

Govan
Did the police know his name in connection with the Murray murders.
Kyle
Yes, since 2023.
Govan
Did they ask him any questions?
Kyle
No, he was never interviewed. He was never questioned.

Up sound ambulance

LINK
By now the police’s shameful conduct has not only been exposed but has just about shattered any prospect of finding justice

Voice over 27
Now a third team of investigators is trying one last time

James Murray
I said to my mother the other day, if this case can still lead to a prosecution these guys will get it there. I don’t know if it can.

Voice over 28
The police have not responded to the questions we sent them.

THE END 14 mins 38 seconds.

PROMO ONE
Voice over
The performance of our law enforcement has been in the spotlight recently

James Murray
I have obviously been privy to what they have done but if you were to write a book on how to not investigate murder you could just run this down, play by play

Voice over
How is the investigation progressing into the double murder of
liquidators Thomas and Cloete Murray


PROMO TWO

Monet Murray
The other day my son asked me daddy where are you.

Voice over
A double murder on the NI highway in the middle of the day and two and a half years later the killers remain at large
Govan
So the investigation into who killed Cloete and Thomas Murray started with mistakes?
Kyle
It starts with a mistake, within hours of the shooting happening.


PROMO THREE
Voice over
Subpoena’s that took months, evidence not collected, prime suspects not interrogated – two police teams that have failed a family

Govan
At that point other people were starting to put together the pieces
was that information reaching the police?
James
Yes, in droves!
Voice over
Can a third police team bring justice to the Murray family?


STUDIO ROR
Rushal Singh is currently behind bars on an unrelated fraud case. He responded via his lawyer that he firmly and unequivocally denies any involvement, knowledge or association with the murders of the Murrays. And that no law enforcement agency has ever questioned him in relation to the murders, nor indicated that he is a person of interest.

Justice Insulted| The Murray Murders 2025 FINAL SCRIPT Fact checked and fixed version for voice over Voice over One In 2023 Cloete Murray was ruffling feathers. One of the country’s top liquidators, he was involved in high profile State Capture cases and other multimillion rand estates. Murray had a nose for finding well hidden assets and cash, a skill that didn’t go down well in the dark tangled criminal landscapes of Gauteng James Murray There is a WhatsApp group of ..I don’t know how to put it, the devil’s favourite children. They don’t necessarily discuss my father, but they discuss all sorts of unsanitary things Voice over 2 James Murray and his younger brother Thomas worked with their father. Title: Saturday 18th March 2023 On a March morning more than two years ago, Thomas joined Cloete to assess three properties of a company called B.I.G- Business Innovations Group that had allegedly defrauded Investec bank of millions. It was Thomas’ first liquidation. His wife Monet was going to join them but stayed at home to look after their 6 month old son Monet Murray He was excited about that, you know he was really crossing his T’s and dotting his I’s. Voice over 3 These are the last known images of Thomas and Cloete, captured by cameras outside the Pretoria home of Rushil Singh one of the B.I.G directors. From this address they’d travelled to the exclusive Melrose Arch shopping district. Govan What stands out for you from that day? Monet Murray Thomas was, he assisted his father with a lot of large matters, dangerous matters, but that week he was very anxious. When he was brushing his teeth, he told me, do you know where to scatter my ashes, and I was like okay well we used to joke around, and he was like “no do you really know where to scatter my ashes. “So, there was something different to him. Voice over 4 At around two in the afternoon, on the N1 highway, near Midrand north of Joburg, a white Ford Ranger pulled up alongside them. Up sound shots 13 bullets were pumped into their vehicle. shots Thomas died on the scene, shot through the heart, the lungs and the arm. Cloete succumbed to his injuries later in hospital. Monet The other day my son asked me daddy where are you? Pappa where are you? Govan Regtig? I have a little cross around my neck, and every night I would tell him, its for Daddy. For pappa, and he would say “kruisie papa” and then he said “Pappa where are you? “That’s difficult! Govan Oh my gosh Monet. James Murray I can only imagine what my brothers last thirty seconds must have been like. I know he was in excruciating pain. They were on the phone with a good friend of my father, and he told me they were laughing and then he heard these cracks, and he just heard my brother scream: eina! Eina! Eina! Govan whispers Ah man… James And then it went silent, and he could just hear my father (breathes) obviously going into some form of instinctive breathing at that point Voice over 5 James and his mother raced to the scene. James Murray We drove as fast as we could hazards on, were just honked the horn. We took the offramp, the big bird offramp. I stopped the vehicle, I jumped out of the car, and I just started running across the highway James I thought it was an accident. Voice over 6 This was the brutal scene that confronted him. James I wasn’t looking at the windows, I was looking at my brother and, on my way back, I realized oh.... those are bullet holes. Voice over 7 Only then did James realise his father and brother had been assassinated. James At that point we didn’t know which one of my father’s high-profile cases was the one that led to this. If you had to ask me on that day, was it the B.I.G case? I would say, I doubt it, there were many other people that wanted my father dead. Voice over 8 The killer is still at large, and a family dealt a double trauma is no closer to finding closure. More than two years later, we ask, why? Fade to black Voice over 9 It was a double murder that made international headlines and rocked the country’s liquidations sector. As speculation on a possible motive for the killing spread, bringing the killers to book fell to Brigadier Pulane (Pauline) Gopane, the head of organized crime in Gauteng. James The joke is what investigation? Voice over 10 At first the family gave Brigadier Gopane’s team the benefit of the doubt, but later they watched them bungle almost every aspect of the investigation James Murray I have obviously been privy to quite a bit of what they have done, but if you were to write a book of how to not investigate murder, you could just run this down, play by play. LINK The Murray murders are an uncomfortable reminder of everything that is wrong in this criminal justice system, and driving past the scene of the assassination, leaves a bitter taste every time. Voice over 11 News24’s investigative journalist, Kyle Cowan, has been following the story for the past two and a half years. The long list of shortcomings began when HE discovered a file in Cloete’s car, mistakenly left behind by the police. Govan So, you assumed the police would have taken it? Kyle That would have been my first thing, go through the car! Ballistic evidence was left behind in the car, the house keys were left behind in the car. That file would have given them, on day one, on the day of the shootings would have told them, these are the people that these guys they were interacting with, minutes, hours, before they were killed. Govan So, the investigation into who killed Cloete and Thomas Murray started with mistakes? Kyle It starts with a mistake within hours of the shootings happening. This file was eventually collected by the family. Voice over 12 From the outset, the investigation, according to Cowan, was beset by delays. Kyle So everything that should take a couple of days, filing subpoenas for cell phone records, takes two months. Voice over 13 Because it was high profile, two officers from the Directorate for Priority Crime, or Hawks, joined the team. A suspect was identified days after the murders. James There was one gent in that team, from the DPCI, that was extremely competent, and he was essentially doing everything, if he wasn’t there, they wouldn’t even have identified Barwell. Kyle They identify a guy called Ryan Barwell. He’s captured on CCTV cameras at Melrose Arch. Up sound Kyle Cowan Cloete Murray and his son Thomas drive in, right behind them is an auctioneer, and the third vehicle is a white Ford Ranger bakkie being driven by Ryan Barwell. Govan So why is he following the Murrays? Kyle What we figured out is that Barwell has very close ties to the same people who the Murray’s were liquidating on behalf of Investec Bank. VO 14 Cameras on the N1 highway also confirmed the vehicle used by the assailants, was a white Ford Ranger. Kyle We are looking at a white Ford Ranger without number plates being driven by Ryan Barwell appearing to follow the Murrays into the Melrose Arch parking garage. Within two hours a same white Ford Ranger is involved in the shooting, and that is captured on camera. VO 15 Shockingly, instead of swiftly acting on the information, James says, Brigadier Gopane removed the Hawks investigators. James Murray And then the investigation grinds to a halt. Govan So she wanted to fire the people doing the work? James That is correct. It was a political exercise VO16 It also emerged that the prime suspect had never been questioned. Govan The police have never interviewed Ryan Barwell. Why not! Kyle Never! I don’t understand to this day why Brig Gopane team failed to interview him. VO 17 Ryan Barwell has a R9 million default judgement against him from SARS, perhaps that’s why WE can’t find him to ask him for his right of reply. Kyle continues Ryan Barwell may not be a suspect in the murders, but he was driving a vehicle that you can forensically match to the vehicle used in the murders – so this person would be your number one witness. He can tell you who was in that car with them that day. At the very least you can exclude him as a suspect. They haven’t even done that! Voice over 18 On the day of their murder, Cloete and Thomas were writing up the assets of the B.I.G group. Two of the company’s directors were Rushil and Nishani Singh. Rushil is a highflyer known for driving high end sports cars. His sister Nishani has since died. James So, they get an arrest warrant for Rushil Singh, they don’t arrest him. It takes them months, they tell us they can’t find him, and they can’t speak to crime intelligence because they don’t trust crime intelligence, so they can’t find him. So, I tell them, he lives with his mother, go to his house, and they just do nothing. Govan At that point other people outside of the police, were starting to put the pieces together. James Yes that is correct. Govan Was that information reaching the police? James Yes, in droves! They had been given notes and information and photos and bank statements, and vehicle transfer records. Voice over 19 It’s evidence, the Murray family believes links the Singh siblings to the assassination. LINK By 2024 the police had been handed the evidence, but instead of acting on it, they chose to do something no one saw coming Voice over 20 James was called in after News 24’s scathing articles about the investigation. He realised then, he was now a suspect, based on his cell phone calls to his brother Thomas. James They knew who drove the vehicle, they know which vehicle did it, they to an extent know who was in the vehicle, at least one of the three people, and at this point based on phone calls between my brother and myself which they think are between my father and myself, they decided that I am a suspect in this murder case, because for some reason they reckon that I would have been a beneficiary of this absolute life destroying event Voice over 21 James filed a complaint to the police, and in what first appeared to be a promising move, the national head of organized crime, Major General Richard Shibiri, was assigned to the case. Kyle At this point he appears to be the guy who can maybe change the fortunes of this investigation. Voice Over 22 But there’s a reason that name sounds familiar. Last month, the Madlanga Commission of Inquiry into corruption and interference in our criminal justice system, heard that General Shibiri is accused of taking bribes in another murder investigation. Accusations he’s strongly denied. Kyle We end 2024 effectively in exactly the same place where we ended the year before. Up sound page turn Kyle The two-year anniversary, by March 2025, the family start becoming angry. Voice over 23 Cowan prepared yet another report, and sent his questions to the police Kyle They then tell me they have recovered the Ford Ranger, the suspect vehicle, the one that was used in the murders. I go to the police impound and I take pictures of the vehicle. That’s in March. They wait until September to start doing anything to this vehicle. Voice over 24 It appears, though, to have been the wrong vehicle. Govan So was that car ever found? Kyle They are never going to find that car Govan. That car is gone Govan Besides the vehicle, they have some idea of who the suspects could be, right? Kyle Yes, so remember back in 2023 people had already figured out Barwell was driving the car, and there are identities of other possible occupants that were given to the police. They have known for two years at this point Voice over 25 This year, an image of the man in the front seat of the Ford Ranger on the day of the murder was published. Govan At this point I am not surprised that they didn’t go and ask him to prove that wasn’t him, leaning forward. Kyle Ya and now they can’t anymore. Govan Why? Kyle Because on the first of October he was killed. Voice over 26 Burnett Hermanus was gunned down outside a Joburg hospital last month. Up sound shots Kyle Burnett Hermanus is the guy we suspect was in the front passenger seat of that white Ford Ranger. The guy who shot them. Govan Did the police know his name in connection with the Murray murders. Kyle Yes, since 2023. Govan Did they ask him any questions? Kyle No, he was never interviewed. He was never questioned. Up sound ambulance LINK By now the police’s shameful conduct has not only been exposed but has just about shattered any prospect of finding justice Voice over 27 Now a third team of investigators is trying one last time James Murray I said to my mother the other day, if this case can still lead to a prosecution these guys will get it there. I don’t know if it can. Voice over 28 The police have not responded to the questions we sent them. THE END 14 mins 38 seconds. PROMO ONE Voice over The performance of our law enforcement has been in the spotlight recently James Murray I have obviously been privy to what they have done but if you were to write a book on how to not investigate murder you could just run this down, play by play Voice over How is the investigation progressing into the double murder of liquidators Thomas and Cloete Murray PROMO TWO Monet Murray The other day my son asked me daddy where are you. Voice over A double murder on the NI highway in the middle of the day and two and a half years later the killers remain at large Govan So the investigation into who killed Cloete and Thomas Murray started with mistakes? Kyle It starts with a mistake, within hours of the shooting happening. PROMO THREE Voice over Subpoena’s that took months, evidence not collected, prime suspects not interrogated – two police teams that have failed a family Govan At that point other people were starting to put together the pieces was that information reaching the police? James Yes, in droves! Voice over Can a third police team bring justice to the Murray family? STUDIO ROR Rushal Singh is currently behind bars on an unrelated fraud case. He responded via his lawyer that he firmly and unequivocally denies any involvement, knowledge or association with the murders of the Murrays. And that no law enforcement agency has ever questioned him in relation to the murders, nor indicated that he is a person of interest. Video

metadata.Summary: It’s been two years and eight months since Cloete Murray and his son Thomas were assassinated on the NI highway near Midrand on a Saturday afternoon. Thomas and his father had been working on a multimillion-rand case for Investec and they had left Melrose Arch and were travelling home. What they did not realize is that they were followed and gunned down by three men in a bakkie near the New Road offramp. The family have been shattered, but they are healing as best they can. The police have been appalling despite promises from two of the nation’s top cops, General Shadrack Sibiya and Richard Shiburi. These two generals promised the family justice after the first law enforcement team failed them. But they have failed them too and now perhaps we know why. In the last few weeks, startling revelations from the Madlanga commission suggest that these men were busy lining their pockets from a man accused of looting Thembisa hospital and attempting to murder his girlfriend. While the allegations remain untested and come from a man accused of serious crimes, the level of detail that were given to three law enforcement officers by Cat Matlala is startling.
metadata.Further information: But back to the Murray family who have revealed that the assassins are known to them as they have the evidence. And yet still no arrests have been made. Carte Blanche goes into the anatomy of an investigation that will reveal the deep flaws in our criminal justice system and tracks the heartbreak and healing of the Murray family over the last 32 months as they have tried everything to get justice and closure. It also looks at the other whistleblowers who have been assassinated in that time.
